title: Cross-Encoder Reranking for Retrieval Precision
description: Implement cross-encoder reranking with Microsoft.Extensions.AI and Semantic Kernel to dramatically improve RAG retrieval quality beyond initial vector search.

data.text: Why Rerank? Bridging Recall and Precision

Bi-encoder vector search is fast but coarse: it computes independent embeddings for the query and each document, then compares with cosine similarity. Cross-encoders are more precise because they jointly encode the query and document together, capturing semantic interactions. The tradeoff is cost — cross-encoders are 10-100x slower per pair. Reranking uses a bi-encoder for initial recall (top-k) and then applies a cross-encoder to re-rank only those k candidates, combining speed with precision.

data.text: In .NET, cross-encoder reranking can be implemented via cloud APIs (Cohere Rerank, Azure AI Search Semantic Ranker) or locally using ONNX Runtime with lightweight cross-encoder models like cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2. The choice depends on latency requirements, data sensitivity, and operational overhead.

data.title: Cloud Reranker with Cohere Rerank API
data.content: Using the Cohere Rerank API for production-quality reranking:

data.text: For data-sensitive deployments, local cross-encoder reranking eliminates cloud API calls. Use ONNX Runtime with models like cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2 (22M parameters, CPU-friendly at ~100ms per pair) or cross-encoder/stsb-roberta-large (340M parameters, ~500ms per pair but higher accuracy).

data.title: Local Cross-Encoder Reranker with ONNX
data.content: Running a quantized cross-encoder locally in .NET:

data.text: Not every retrieval result benefits from reranking. When the initial vector search returns high-confidence results (e.g., cosine similarity > 0.9), skip reranking to save latency and cost. Conversely, when results are borderline, apply a stricter cross-encoder threshold. The threshold is domain-dependent — test empirically.

Use a lightweight classifier to predict whether reranking will change the top-5 order. If the classifier predicts no change (with 95% confidence), skip the expensive cross-encoder entirely. This can reduce reranking cost by 40-60% without measurable accuracy loss.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cross-encoders jointly encode query and document, capturing richer semantic interactions than bi-encoders
Use cloud rerankers (Cohere) for highest quality, ONNX for local/data-sensitive deployments
Set skip thresholds: if top-k vector results exceed similarity threshold, skip reranking
Rerank only top-50 to top-100 from vector search — not the entire corpus
Cross-encoder reranking adds 5-15% to RAG accuracy at 10-50ms additional latency
data.takeaway: Reranking is a precision-boosting technique that spends additional compute only on the most promising candidates, making it a cost-effective way to improve RAG quality.
